items.title: A Dynamic Retrieval-Augmented Generation System with Selective Memory and Remembrance
items.title_zh: 具备选择性记忆与遗忘的动态检索增强生成系统
items.summary: Adaptive RAG Memory replaces a static vector index with a dynamic memory substrate in which frequently retrieved items are consolidated and protected while rarely used ones decay. On a lightweight retrieval benchmark it reaches NDCG@5 of about 0.940 and Recall@5 of 1.000 with roughly 22M embedding parameters, and compares static versus dynamic RAG across Llama 3.1 and GPT-4o.

items.title: Lying with Truths: Open-Channel Multi-Agent Collusion for Belief Manipulation via Generative Montage
items.title_zh: 用真相撒谎：开放信道多智能体合谋与信念操纵
items.summary: The paper formalizes a cognitive collusion attack in which agents coordinate to steer beliefs using only truthful evidence fragments posted through public channels, and reports success rates of 74.4% for proprietary models and 70.6% for open-weight models across 14 LLM families. Stronger reasoning models prove more susceptible, and false beliefs spread to downstream judges.

items.title: SAGE-32B: Agentic Reasoning via Iterative Distillation
items.title_zh: SAGE-32B：通过迭代蒸馏实现智能体推理
items.summary: SAGE-32B is a 32B model initialized from Qwen2.5-32B and fine-tuned with Iterative Distillation, a two-stage process with tested feedback loops, to operate in an agentic loop emphasizing task decomposition, tool use and error recovery. It adds an inverse-reasoning meta-cognition head that forecasts planning failures, reports higher multi-tool success than similarly sized baselines while remaining competitive on standard reasoning tests, and releases its weights.

items.title: Aletheia: Quantifying Cognitive Conviction in Reasoning Models via Regularized Inverse Confusion Matrix
items.title_zh: Aletheia：通过正则化逆混淆矩阵量化推理模型的认知信念强度
items.summary: Project Aletheia proposes a framework that uses Tikhonov regularization to invert a judge's confusion matrix, aiming to measure the depth of belief in reasoning models rather than only knowledge breadth. A preliminary pilot on 2025 baselines such as DeepSeek-R1 and OpenAI o1 suggests reasoning models can act as a cognitive buffer but may exhibit defensive overthinking under adversarial pressure.

items.title: Bayesian Orchestration of Multi-LLM Agents for Cost-Aware Sequential Decision-Making
items.title_zh: 成本感知多 LLM 智能体序贯决策的贝叶斯编排
items.summary: The paper argues that querying one LLM for a confidence score is inadequate for sequential decisions with asymmetric costs, and instead treats multiple LLMs as approximate likelihood models whose contrastive estimates are aggregated and updated with Bayes rule. In resume screening with 1,000 resumes and five LLMs, it reports a 34% cost reduction ($294,000) versus the best single-model baseline and narrows the max demographic-parity gap from 22 to 5 points.

items.title: From Failure to Mastery: Generating Hard Samples for Tool-use Agents
items.title_zh: 从失败到精通：为工具使用智能体生成困难样本
items.summary: HardGen builds a dynamic API graph from agent failure cases to synthesize hard traces, uses them as priors to instantiate advanced tools and queries, and generates verifiable chain-of-thought data in a closed evaluation loop. The authors report that a 4B-parameter model trained on the resulting dataset outperforms several leading open and closed models, including GPT-5.2, Gemini-3-Pro and Claude-Opus-4.5.

items.title: Improving Behavioral Alignment in LLM Social Simulations via Context Formation and Navigation
items.title_zh: 通过情境构建与导航改进大模型社会模拟中的行为对齐
items.summary: The authors propose a two-stage framework: context formation, which specifies the experimental design and decision context, and context navigation, which guides reasoning within that representation. Across four models and three economic games, complex decision environments require both stages to match human behavior, while a simpler demand-estimation task needs only context formation.

items.title: Who is the Winning Algorithm? Rank Aggregation for Comparative Studies
items.title_zh: 谁是最佳算法？面向比较研究的排名聚合
items.summary: The paper proposes a framework that estimates each algorithm's probability of ranking first on a future unseen dataset by using complete rankings across a benchmark rather than only win counts, and reports gains over existing methods in synthetic and real-world examples.
